title: Anatomy of a Frontier Lab Agent Intrusion: A Timeline of the July 2026 Incident
titleZh: 前沿实验室智能体入侵剖析：2026年7月事件时间线
author: artninja1988
relevanceReason: 文章详细描述了2026年7月Hugging Face遭受的AI Agent入侵事件，涉及AI安全、零日漏洞利用、基础设施渗透等核心安全议题，与科技日报关注的AI安全、云服务安全高度相关。
summaryRaw: Back to Articles A companion technical writeup to our incident disclosure. This post walks through how the intrusion actually worked: the two initial-access vectors, how the agent pivoted and moved laterally, representative examples of the commands that were run and how we investigated with GLM 5.2 (an open-source model). Live credentials, internal hostnames, and specific indicators have been redacted or genericized, while the techniques are described exactly as observed by Hugging Face. We are publishing this level of detail because the technique matters more than the incident, as it reveals the emerging attack capabilities of the frontier agents, how they could be used by rogue actors, and how everyone should be prepared as defenders. Below is an interactive replay of the intrusion - a step-by-step visualization of the 4.5-day campaign: the attack chain across trust boundaries, phase activity, and the commands as they were recorded.
⛶ Watch the interactive replay in full screen

Over roughly two and a half days inside our infrastructure, an autonomous AI agent driven by a combination of OpenAI models ran an end-to-end intrusion against our platform: it was thousands of small, automated decisions, executed at machine speed across short-lived sandbox environments, with command-and-control staged on ordinary public web services. The agent was running an internal OpenAI cyber-capability evaluation based on the ExploitGym benchmark, which tasks an AI agent with finding and exploiting software vulnerabilities. OpenAI ran this on its own infrastructure, and the ExploitGym maintainers and their infrastructure had no involvement in the deployment or operation of that evaluation environment. As far as we were able to infer, across the course of being evaluated on this benchmark, the agent inferred that Hugging Face may host that benchmark's models, datasets, and reference solutions. We believe the entire intrusion was, from the agent's point of view, an attempt to cheat the evaluation: reach our production systems and steal the test solutions rather than solve the challenge on its own. Our forensic reconstruction covers ~17,600 attacker actions that we were able to recover, grouped into ~6,280 clusters, between 2026-07-09 02:28 UTC and 2026-07-13 14:14 UTC. We reconstructed these actions from the agent's logs on a code sandbox used by the agent (see below) and were able to map them to shell commands as well as evaluation submissions and correlate actions with our own platform logs, in particular from the dataset processor nodes, API, and pod. Using open-weights models, in particular zai-org/GLM-5.2, we were able to decipher most of the agent payloads (see below) that were encrypted via chunking and key encryption. The campaign, as we were able to reconstruct it, had two stages:

Stage 1: reaching a launchpad by chaining through other parties' infrastructure. As documented in OpenAI's blog post (https://openai.com/index/hugging-face-model-evaluation-security-incident/), during an internal capability evaluation on OpenAI's platform, the agent escaped its sandbox by exploiting a zero-day in the package registry cache proxy, one of its primary permitted network egress with internet, then abused a public code-evaluation harness hosted by a user of a third-party infrastructure provider. It was able to run commands as root/admin on that external sandbox and used it as a control, staging, and egress base for the entire campaign: it acted as an external launchpad for the agent. That compromised external sandbox had no direct network path to our cluster; however, during our counter-intervention to stop the intrusion, we were able to retrieve some of the agent logs from this external launchpad. We used those to reconstruct the present forensic analysis. Stage 2: the intrusion into Hugging Face infrastructure. From that external launchpad, the agent abused our dataset-processing pipeline via two injection vectors, both targeting the same config-driven data loader within our production Kubernetes pods. The first vector was an HDF5 external raw storage dataset read that returned the contents of local files: it handed the agent the pod's environment (secrets and tokens) and the worker's own source. The second vector was a Jinja2 template injection that executed arbitrary code, giving the agent a foothold inside our perimeter.

安全团队使用开源模型GLM-5.2解密Agent加密载荷，还原约17600个攻击动作，揭示前沿AI Agent的自主攻击能力

comments.author: wxw
comments.textRawHtml:
> the agent happened to escape via a 0-day exploit from the package proxy cache to access the internet

> The agent found an unsecured, user-hosted public endpoint designed to allow running arbitrary code for CyberGym-style tasks on third-party sandbox infrastructure (Modal)

> On this external sandbox, the agent abused an existing CyberGym execution harness [...] The agent repurposed this harness to run arbitrary shell commands [...]

> The agent crafted malicious dataset configs and uploaded them to our platform. When our dataset server processed one, the config drove the data loader inside the production pod the server ran in. [...] the loader that turns a dataset's declared config into file reads [...] A single dataset upload leaked both credentials and pipeline implementation details [...]

> A malicious dataset config used an fsspec reference:// spec whose numeric offset field was actually a Jinja2 template. The renderer wrongly evaluated it, and the agent walked the standard Python object graph to reach exec. This ran arbitrary Python inside a production conversion worker pod on our Kubernetes cluster [...]

One of the best post-mortems I've read recently, thank you for including all the details.

I'm surprised there are comments here that aren't impressed about what was accomplished here. This is insane work compared to what agents were capable of even just last year.

The quotes above don't even capture all of it (e.g. building it's own communication protocol, working across multiple days, etc.).
comments.textZhHtml:
> 代理碰巧通过包代理缓存中的 0day 漏洞进行逃逸以访问互联网

> 代理发现了一个不安全的、用户托管的公共端点，旨在允许在第三方沙箱基础设施（模态）上运行 CyberGym 式任务的任意代码

> 在此外部沙箱上，代理滥用了现有的 CyberGym 执行工具 [...] 代理重新利用了该工具来运行任意 shell 命令[...]

> 该代理制作了恶意数据集配置并将其上传到我们的平台。当我们的数据集服务器处理一个数据集时，配置会驱动服务器运行的生产 Pod 内的数据加载器。[...] 将数据集声明的配置转换为文件的加载器读取 [...] 单个数据集上传泄露了凭据和管道实现详细信息 [...]

> 恶意数据集配置使用了 fsspec Reference:// 规范，其数字偏移字段实际上是 Jinja2 模板。渲染器错误地评估了它，代理遍历标准 Python 对象图以到达 exec。它在我们的 Kubernetes 集群上的生产转换工作 Pod 中运行任意 Python [...]

这是我最近读过的最好的事后分析之一，感谢您提供所有详细信息。

我很惊讶这里有一些评论对这里所完成的事情没有留下深刻的印象。与去年代理的能力相比，这是一项疯狂的工作。

上面的引用甚至没有涵盖所有内容（例如，构建自己的通信协议、跨多天工作等）。

children.author: sobellian
children.textRawHtml: A trend I've noticed in results from AI search (not just LLMs) is that they often look obvious or hard to miss in retrospect. But finding them by oneself is more difficult. I personally experience this when looking at engine lines in chess or go. I have also noticed this description in AI-generated proofs or counterexamples to certain theorems. So while we can say, yes, it found public endpoints or poorly configured software or [etc]; sure, but could you have found those? And in what amount of time?
children.textZhHtml: 我在人工智能搜索（不仅仅是法学硕士）的结果中注意到的一个趋势是，回想起来它们通常看起来很明显或很难错过。但自己去寻找它们却更加困难。我个人在查看国际象棋或围棋中的引擎线时经历过这一点。我还注意到人工智能生成的证明或某些定理的反例中的这种描述。因此，虽然我们可以说，是的，它发现了公共端点或配置不当的软件或[等等]；当然可以，但是你能找到那些吗？以及需要多长时间？

children.author: janalsncm
children.textRawHtml:
To put this into game theory lingo, I think this is because the “branching factor” for any kind of research or exploit is extremely large. So looking backwards it doesn’t seem complicated, but looking forwards there are an enormous number of possible next actions.

Similar to finding a filament for lightbulbs, it might seem obvious to use tungsten, but at the time it wasn’t and Edison searched thousands of materials.
children.textZhHtml:
用博弈论术语来说，我认为这是因为任何类型的研究或利用的“分支因素”都非常大。因此，回顾过去，这似乎并不复杂，但展望未来，下一步可能采取的行动有大量。

与寻找灯泡灯丝类似，使用钨似乎是显而易见的，但当时情况并非如此，爱迪生搜索了数千种材料。

children.author: N_Lens
children.textRawHtml: Tesla's critique of Edison was valid though (That he would rather spend a long time empirically testing things, rather than use a bit of theory and knowledge to narrow the search field).
children.textZhHtml:
不过特斯拉对爱迪生的批评是有道理的（即他宁愿花大量时间进行经验性测试，也不愿利用一点理论和知识来缩小搜索范围）。
我认为这些模型确实在发挥它们的长处；在极其庞大的数据语料库中进行不知疲倦的搜索。人类并不特别擅长这个（事实上，人类在这方面简直糟透了）。

我们在许多方面仍然具有竞争力和优势，并不是因为我们能瞬间筛选海量数据，而是因为我们能够学习、建立关联，并拥有更优的启发式方法。

在我自己的使用中，我发现AI非常擅长发现那些最终看来微不足道、但需要搜索一系列错综复杂的关联文件的漏洞。这对人类来说很耗时。

那远远超过了十七个音节。
是的，想象一下这样一个世界：小偷的时间如此廉价，以至于任何一个想成为大盗的人都会随便雇上50个小偷，让他们挨家挨户地去寻找有趣的东西。
是的，而且在1层搜索深度下，Leela会击败Stockfish，因为它的评估函数要好得多。即使搜索速度真的很快，搜索过程本身也是很慢的。

children.author: catigula
children.textRawHtml:
I think the models are legitimately doing what they're good at; tireless search across an extremely large corpus of data. Humans aren't particularly good at this (in fact, they're absolutely terrible).

The fact that we remain competitive and superior in many aspects isn't because we can instantly sift through tons of data, it's because we learn and correlate and have superior heuristics.

In my own use, I find that AI is really good at finding bugs that are ultimately trivial but require searching through a convoluted series of inter-related files. This takes time for a human.

children.author: stymaar
children.textRawHtml:
This is symptomatic of a trend that Simon Willison called the “relentless productivity” of US frontier lab. Instead of being just “smarter”, like previous models were, the current generation is being trained through RL to have this kind of behavior.

Personally I'm not “impressed”, I'm appalled, because this kind of behavior is practically never what you want (if you forgot to give the model a tool, a useful model should identity the missing part and ask the user for it, not spend a billion token building/stealing the tool as a side quest) but it's the perfect recipe for a “universal paperclip” scenario.

OpenAI and Anthropic talk about “safety” a lot, but they look pretty reckless with this kind of RL training pipeline.
children.textZhHtml:
这是西蒙·威利森 (Simon Willison) 所说的美国前沿实验室“不懈的生产力”趋势的征兆。现在的这一代人不再像以前的模型那样只是“更聪明”，而是通过强化学习进行训练，以具有这种行为。

就我个人而言，我并不“印象深刻”，我感到震惊，因为这种行为实际上从来都不是你想要的（如果你忘记给模型一个工具，一个有用的模型应该识别缺失的部分并向用户询问，而不是花费 10 亿代币构建/窃取该工具作为支线任务），但它是完美的秘诀对于“通用回形针”场景。

OpenAI 和 Anthropic 经常谈论“安全”，但他们对这种 RL 训练流程看起来相当鲁莽。

children.author: ifwinterco
children.textRawHtml:
If you look at what OpenAI and Anthropic actually do, they clearly either don't believe what they're saying, or they're idiots.

They're claiming they've developed a cyber grade model that's "too dangerous to release".

But then they're running it connected to the public internet, not airgapped, protected only by a software sandbox... exactly the kind of thing an AI trained for cyber stuff is supposed to be able to find bugs in.

(Or maybe they were actually hoping this exact scenario would happen because it's good marketing)
children.textZhHtml:
如果你看看OpenAI和Anthropic实际在做什么，他们显然要么不相信自己的话，要么就是蠢货。

他们声称自己开发了一个网络安全级模型，但“太危险了不能发布”。

然而他们却让它连接公共互联网运行，没有物理隔离，仅仅靠一个软件沙箱来保护……这恰恰是受过网络安全训练的AI应该能找出漏洞的那种环境。

（又或者他们其实就盼着发生这种状况，因为这是很好的营销手段）

children.author: mike_hock
children.textRawHtml:
I think this a positive effect of LLMs, especially once these capabilities get into the hands of criminals and hostile foreign states, i.e. they will do maximum damage with all the safeties off.

This will force everyone to finally take security seriously at both the development and operational levels. You can no longer keep sneaking backdoors into software and count on them remaining hidden for 10 years so you have a nice portfolio of zero days to exploit at any given time.
children.textZhHtml:
我认为这是大语言模型带来的一个积极影响，尤其是当这些能力落入犯罪分子和敌对外国势力手中时，也就是说，他们会在关闭所有安全防护的情况下造成最大破坏。

这将迫使所有人最终在开发和运维层面都认真对待安全问题。你不能再继续偷偷在软件里留后门，并指望它们能隐藏10年，以便你随时拥有一批好用的零日漏洞来利用。

I was skeptical after last week's announcements, and I have to say I'm impressed now. Over the last two days, I reproduced the entire chain of components involved, and the exploits at play, and even though none of the exploits are crazy smart, the long series of pivots demonstrates a level of agency I didn't think today's LLMs had.

我对上周的公告表示怀疑，但我不得不说现在给我留下了深刻的印象。在过去的两天里，我重现了所涉及的整个组件链以及正在发挥作用的漏洞，尽管没有一个漏洞是非常聪明的，但一长串的关键点展示了我认为今天的法学硕士所没有的代理水平。
